citations.quote: In the adopted frequency-diagonal Fock interpretation, the positive-frequency Fourier coefficient of the ordered current two-point function is $\omega/2$ times the mode occupation. Thus the occupation associated with spectral coefficient $S_k(\omega)$ is, by this model's normalization, $2S_k(\omega)/\omega$ for $\omega>0$. This identification is part of the adopted channel model; it is not a detector response or an observed particle count.

Adopt the scattering and local-decay assumption that for each fixed $K$, these bounded sesquilinear forms converge in operator norm as $s\to+\infty$ to the direct integral of the exponential near-horizon channel and the independent incoming vacuum channel mixed by the displayed passive map. Explicitly, operator-norm convergence means $$\sup_{\|f\|_2,\|g\|_2\le1}|B_{\ell,s}(f,g)-B_{\ell,\infty}(f,g)|\longrightarrow0.$$

Its Fourier spectrum, using $\widehat C_k(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}C_k(s)e^{-i\omega s}\,ds$ in the distributional sense, is $$S_k(\omega)=\frac{\omega}{2(e^{2\pi\omega/k}-1)}\quad(\omega\ne0),\qquad S_k(0)=\frac{k}{4\pi}.$$

Define the output occupation as the quadratic-form expectation $\mathfrak n_{\rm out}(\omega):=\|b_\omega\Psi_\omega\|^2$ of the number operator $b_\omega^\dagger b_\omega$. Then $\mathfrak n_{\rm out}(\omega)=\Gamma(\omega)n_\omega$.
For the Planck occupation function $n_\theta(\omega)=(\exp(\theta\omega)-1)^{-1}$ with width $\theta>0$ measured in seconds, one has $n_\theta(\omega)>0$ for every $\omega>0$.

The associated geometric surface-gravity parameter in inverse metres and its time-frequency version are, by this model's normalization, $$\kappa_{\rm geom}:=\frac{1}{2r_s}=\frac{c^2}{4GM},\qquad k:=c\kappa_{\rm geom}=\frac{c^3}{4GM}>0.$$

derivations.claim: The adopted spectral normalization identifies the input occupation as 2S_k(omega)/omega. Substituting the supplied exponential-channel spectrum gives n_theta(omega)=(exp(theta omega)-1)^-1. The passive-map number identity is linear in the input state; expanding b^dagger b and using the independent vacuum makes its environment and cross terms vanish, leaving Gamma_l(omega)n_theta(omega). Frequency-diagonal integration against |f|^2 gives the finite-packet integral.

The operator-norm convergence of the outgoing number forms implies convergence of each diagonal packet pairing, since the packet has L2 norm one; therefore its limit is the integral computed in step 1.1.

On the common compact band away from zero, g(omega)=Gamma_l(omega)n_theta(omega) is bounded and continuous. Weak concentration of the normalized packet measures at omega_0 makes their mass outside every neighborhood of omega_0 tend to zero; the displayed epsilon bound therefore proves convergence of the integral to g(omega_0).
Taking the late-time limit first and the packet-concentration limit second gives Gamma_l(omega_0)/(exp(2 pi omega_0/k)-1); no finite-width packet is replaced by its central-frequency value.

Matching theta omega with hbar omega/(k_B T_infinity) and substituting k=c^3/(4GM) gives T_infinity=hbar c^3/(8 pi G M k_B); dimensional reduction gives kelvins. This parameter remains a model prediction, not an observation.
